description: harmonize-wq is a Python package published by the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency for preparing Water Quality Portal observations. It identifies differences in units, sampling methods and chemical representation, applies documented cleaning choices, and reshapes long result tables into wider analysis tables. These outputs can provide comparable observations for calibrating water-quality or treatment-process simulations. The intended data source is the United States Water Quality Portal, while coverage and sampling periods remain specific to each monitoring programme. The source and demonstrations are freely available on GitHub under MIT. A limitation is that the tool cannot decide whether observations meet a particular study’s quality requirements; domain experts must choose acceptance thresholds and inspect flagged changes. No directly related catalogue record was established. This review checked the repository and the published software summary without retrieving monitoring observations or assessing a treatment model.
